subject: humanities
passage: Pansori, a Korean form of musical storytelling, requires only two performers: a singer, who narrates a long tale through song, speech, and gesture, and a drummer, who keeps time on a barrel drum and calls out short shouts of encouragement known as chuimsae. A complete performance of a single story can last several hours. Audiences are expected to take part as well, and experienced listeners time ______ own shouts carefully, calling out at the end of a phrase rather than in the middle of one, so that the cries spur the singer on instead of interrupting the song.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The shouts belong to "experienced listeners," a plural noun. A plural antecedent needs the plural possessive pronoun "their." The singular nouns nearby, such as "the singer" and "a drummer," are not the ones timing these shouts.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Its" is singular and refers to a thing, but the shouts belong to the plural "listeners."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "His or her" is singular, but the antecedent "experienced listeners" is plural.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "One's" refers to a general, unnamed person, but the antecedent is the specific plural "listeners."
